absent: Numeric encodings of huge page sizes, shifts, orders, protection bits, marker values, and fault flag bits.
Full layouts of control structures such as address spaces, areas, folios, page tables, notifier ranges, gather contexts, and cgroup objects.
Initialisation, teardown, and sharing setup for middle directories and internals of table walk, allocation, and unshare helpers.
Reservation accounting, policy node selection, page cache insertion, reverse mapping, and usage charging internals beyond the call sites shown.
Scheduling, error recovery, and concurrency guarantees beyond the observed lock acquisition and release ordering.
Caller side protocol and flag definitions driving poison, continue, and copy retries outside the shown entry points.

findings.text: The move tables helper advances a source and destination address together by one huge page stride, skips missing tables and empty slots, abandons shared middle directory blocks that fail to unshare, allocates each destination slot, transfers the entry, queues a translation removal, and reports progress as distance advanced before any allocation stop.

Table mutation paths open a device notification interval widened when middle directory sharing is possible, take the area write guard before the file mapping write guard, hold a gather context across the loop, use per slot table locks inside, flush only translations, then release in reverse order and close the interval and gather context.

A zap prologue does nothing when the area lacks a backing file, otherwise widens the interval for possible sharing and acquires area then mapping write guards; the matching epilogue either frees the area guard on final unmap so the area becomes ineligible for sharing before the mapping guard is released, or simply releases both guards in reverse order.

The atomic fill entry supports poison, continue and copy request modes: poison plants a poison marker only into an empty slot, continue attaches to an already cached folio, and copy allocates a fresh folio and brings user bytes into it, with shared areas additionally checked against cache presence and file size before insertion.

Copy moves through allocation, user copy, cache insertion, locked installation and accounting states; when the user copy cannot complete while locked it releases the fresh folio, preserves the reservation, saves a policy placed temporary folio for the caller to fill outside the lock, and resumes later by allocating the final folio and moving bulk bytes from the temporary.

Installation refuses to overwrite occupied slots except fault markers, rejects hardware poisoned folios, requires up to date state with a barrier for newly filled folios, chooses file versus new anonymous reverse mapping by cache membership, suppresses writability for protected requests and private continue, always marks dirty and young, optionally sets the fault indication, then updates the cache without invalidation because the prior state was non present.

The folio copy helper walks each constituent base page, briefly maps it locally, optionally suppresses faults around the user copy, unmaps, subtracts successfully moved bytes from the remaining count, stops on first short copy, maintains data cache coherence for completed pages, and yields the processor between pages.

The protection walk validates a non empty interval, widens notification for possible sharing, flushes caches, gathers translation state, then visits each huge slot, treats absent, empty, poisoned, migrating and marker states distinctly from present entries, removes translations for changed present mappings, and returns either a base page count derived from changed slots or a negative allocation failure.

Write protection requests allocate missing tables solely to plant a fault marker while read protection requests skip allocation, present entries gain or lose the fault indication according to set versus resolve flags, resolve clears a lone fault marker back to empty, and areas with read protection active coerce any fault marked present entry back to inaccessible protection.

Hardware poisoned and poison marker slots are left untouched by protection changes, migrating entries are downgraded from writable to readable form, and any middle directory unsharing observed while fault protection flags are active is treated as unexpected.

The huge offset lookup descends through top, fourth, upper and middle levels, reports absence when an intermediate level is not present, returns the upper level slot itself when the requested size matches that level, otherwise returns the middle level slot.

The poison query serialised by the global huge lock reports whether a folio is a huge folio and, when it is, succeeds immediately for already freed folios, attempts a reference for migratable folios or when unpoisoning is requested, and otherwise reports busy.

One helper unshares middle directories across the whole area after aligning its bounds to the upper directory size while taking locks, and another clears recorded huge reservations but only for areas already recognised as huge page areas.

Control file identifiers pack an offset in upper bits with a size in lower bits, with small extractors recovering each half and a constructor shifting a structure offset and combining the field size; two template counts are defined as the element counts of default and legacy file tables.

Each control group initialises per size fault and reservation counters linked to the parent counters, enables failure counting only outside the default hierarchy, and caps each counter at the largest multiple of that size pages per huge page fitting below the generic maximum; usage means any fault counter reads non zero.

Group creation allocates a flexible object with per node pointers, records the first group as root, allocates per node accounting preferring the local node with fallback for offline nodes, initialises counters, and frees everything on failure; offline repeatedly migrates every active folio charge to the parent or to an uncapped root until no usage remains, ignoring folios not owned by the departing group.

Offline scanning holds the global huge spin lock with interrupts disabled while walking each size active list and reschedules between full sweeps until drained, and the poison query holds the same interrupt disabling lock across its flag tests and reference attempt.

Temporary folios used to stage user bytes for a later retry use policy derived node placement but with fallback disabled so the per node pool cannot be breached, and the associated policy reference is always released.
